title: BBQ Breakfast Hash
subtitle: Leftover BBQ pulled into a cast-iron hash with eggs on top.
description: Pulled pork or brisket folded into crispy potato hash with eggs cracked on top. Leftover BBQ becomes a breakfast the crew votes for — extra sauce on the side.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for BBQ Breakfast Hash in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Crisp the potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat cast iron over medium-high with oil. Add potatoes in one layer; let them sit 4 minutes before tossing for crust. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Warm the BBQ
steps.instruction: Fold in onion and pulled pork with a splash of BBQ sauce. Heat through without drying the meat. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Eggs on top
steps.instruction: Make wells in the hash. Crack eggs in, cover until whites set. Finish with cheese if using. Plan about 6 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Serve with extra sauce
steps.instruction: Serve straight from the skillet with extra BBQ sauce on the side for the crew. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
